newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end higher, but off peaks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end higher, but off peaks.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed higher, but back from their morning highs, in active trade on Wednesday as persistent profit-taking pressure prevented the index from challenging for a higher upside, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 24.51 points or 0.38 percent higher at 6,538.24. Turnover was a heavy T$50.20 billion.
The index had reached an intra-day high of 6,569.34 points on buying from investors who brokers said were hoping to rally the market out of its recent consolidation.
"But at the 6,550 level it is apparent that selling pressure remains strong," said George Hou of Jardine Fleming.
"There was a strong early-session attempt to break the resistance, but eventually the momentum was lost," Hou added.

The plastics sector led the market, gaining 0.84 percent on reports of international price hikes for petrochemical products polypropylene and polyethylene. USI Far East soared the daily seven percent limit or T$2.20 to T$34.80.
Shares in the financial sector rose 0.45 percent behind the strong listing debut of state-run Central Insurance, which also went limit up to close at T$51.
"Those two sectors guided the market today, enabling it to stay up despite selling pressure," Hou said.
Electronics shares, which had risen lately on strong buying by foreign investors, fought off profit-taking sentiment to gain 0.26 percent.
Brokers said they expected the market to continue a gradual uptrend in the near term, but no significant jump was seen.
They predicted a 6,500-6,560 range for Thursday.
